## Welcome to your practice report

This is a **Quarto** document.
It mixes prose text with R code and output.
When you render it,
Quarto runs the code below and builds a finished HTML page.

Change `author: "Your Name"` in the header above to your own name,
then render this file.

## Packages

Load every package the report uses once, at the top:
the tidyverse for data and charts,
`tidymodels` for modelling,
and `medicaldata` for example datasets.

```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
library(tidymodels)
library(medicaldata)
```

## A first look at the data

`data/patients.csv` is a small practice dataset of 12 synthetic patients,
from
[`ehsanx/HDSx-workspace`](https://github.com/ehsanx/HDSx-workspace/blob/7e3d2f65348f3ac689be41dfaefb7eaf1c04fb2a/data/patients.csv).
The code chunk below reads it and shows the first few rows.

```{r}
patients <- read.csv("data/patients.csv")
head(patients)
```

## A first chart

```{r}
ggplot(patients, aes(x = age)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Number of patients")
```

## A second chart

```{r}
ggplot(patients, aes(x = age, y = systolic_bp, colour = diabetes)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Systolic blood pressure (mm Hg)",
       colour = "Diabetes")
```

## A medicaldata dataset

`medicaldata` has 15 medical datasets to explore,
each described on the
[package website](https://higgi13425.github.io/medicaldata/reference/).

::: {.callout-note}
The website also lists a few newer datasets
that the installed version (0.2.0, from CRAN) doesn't have yet.
Run `data(package = "medicaldata")` to see the ones you can load.

To get the newer datasets too,
install the development version from GitHub in the R terminal,
then restart R:

```{r}
#| eval: false
remotes::install_github("higgi13425/medicaldata")
```
:::

`covid_testing` holds deidentified COVID-19 test results from 2020.

```{r}
ggplot(covid_testing, aes(x = age)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 5) +
  labs(x = "Age (years)", y = "Number of tests")
```

## A quick model

`licorice_gargle` comes from a randomised trial (Ruetzler et al., 2013)
where patients gargled either licorice or sugar water before surgery
and were asked about sore throat afterwards.
We fit a logistic regression to compare the odds of a sore throat
30 minutes after surgery.
An odds ratio below 1 means fewer sore throats with licorice.

```{r}
licorice <- licorice_gargle |>
  mutate(
    gargle = factor(treat, levels = c(0, 1), labels = c("sugar", "licorice")),
    sore_throat = factor(pacu30min_throatPain > 0, levels = c(FALSE, TRUE),
                         labels = c("no", "yes"))
  ) |>
  drop_na(sore_throat)

logistic_reg() |>
  fit(sore_throat ~ gargle, data = licorice) |>
  tidy(exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE)
```
